summary.text: 高 is a pictograph of a tall structure, traditionally understood as a raised building or viewing tower. It represents “high” or “tall,” its common meaning today.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a tall structure, traditionally described as a raised building or viewing tower. The traditional analysis into 冂 and 口 does not establish that either shape had a separate role in the original picture.

components.text: Treat 高 as one picture of a tall structure. A traditional analysis separates it into 冂 and 口, but their separate original meanings and roles are not established.

history.text: Catalogues record 高 in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, as well as later scripts. These records establish a broad history of written forms, but the available descriptions do not show specific changes between them or establish the early examples’ lexical contexts.
高 is graphically compared with 京, which is also described as depicting a tall structure. Their resemblance does not establish that either character derives from the other or that 京 is part of 高.
高 is the standard form; 髙 is recorded as a variant.

uncertainties.text: The tall-structure interpretation is supported, but the exact architecture depicted and the earliest securely established word sense remain unresolved. The traditional analysis into 冂 and 口 does not establish separate original contributions from those shapes.
No definite graphic or lexical relationship between 高 and 京, or definite lexical relationship between 高 and 喬, is established here. No phonetic component or whole-character borrowing is proposed.

senses.text: The traditional pictographic interpretation connects the tall structure with “high.” No verified inscription context securely establishes this as the earliest attested lexical sense.
The common current meaning is “high” or “tall.”

senses.gloss: high place or ridge; excellence, esteem, high price, old age, or a high or forceful voice
senses.text: Textual citations and dictionary records attest these uses, but do not establish when they arose or how they developed from “high” or “tall.” Their pathways are left unspecified.

limitations.text: The traditional account links the tall-building picture to “high,” but the earliest lexical sense and chronology of that connection are not securely established by a dated inscription context.
Historical uses such as “excellent,” “esteemed,” “expensive,” “old,” and “loud” are recorded, but their dates and semantic pathways are not established.

overview.text: 高 is one picture of a tall structure used for the idea “high” or “tall.” The traditional account supports this reading, though the earliest word sense is not securely dated.

components.text: Read the whole graph as a tall structure. The traditional split into 冂 and 口 does not establish separate meanings for those shapes.
